paper.title: LVOmniBench: Pioneering Long Audio-Video Understanding Evaluation for Omnimodal LLMs

evidence.section: Abstract; benchmark construction and statistics; task taxonomy
evidence.paraphrase: 275 manually curated videos of 10-90 minutes (mean 34m29s, 6-20x longer than prior audio-video benchmarks) with 1,014 QA pairs across 9 task subcategories spanning perception, understanding, inference and logical reasoning. The abstract states the benchmark targets 'long-term memory, temporal localization, fine-grained understanding, and multimodal perception', so QA requires recalling and cross-referencing audio (speech 763 / sound 137 / music 114) and visual evidence separated by tens of minutes.

adjudication_notes: Scored memory_adjacent: it evaluates long-horizon audio-visual context comprehension of OmniLLMs and explicitly names long-term memory as a target ability, but it does not make agent memory architecture or memory management the central object of evaluation, and it prescribes no memory read/write protocol.
primary_modality set to video_streaming because the persistent experience under test is the tens-of-minutes video stream; audio is co-present and recorded as a secondary modality.
